websearch.worst: B: Summary presents DRIFT as a separate larger trial registered to fill the gap, though the DRIFT protocol (same 3-day 80% restriction, ~34% deficit design as the Annals trial) appears to be the protocol of that very trial
websearch.worst_summary_quote: a larger 52-week trial (DRIFT) was registered to address that gap
websearch.worst_page_quote: This 80% energy restriction on three fast days per week translates to a targeted weekly energy deficit of ~34%.
websearch.reader_gets_wrong: A reader would think the 12-month Annals result is one trial and that a separate, larger, still-pending trial will settle the question, when the Annals trial likely is the DRIFT trial.
websearch.notes: Annals paper not in links; PMC protocol and Medical Dialogues compared; HealthDay/Newsweek/Scimex/ClinicalTrials gave no usable text. Omitted: 58% vs 47% reaching 5% loss, cardiometabolic secondary results, 300 min/week exercise and behavioral support in both arms. Newsweek ease-of-maintenance claim: maybe from an unfetched page. Identity of Annals trial with DRIFT inferred from matching design, not from an explicit statement in fetched text.

webfetch.fetch_prompt: Does this article report randomized trials comparing intermittent fasting with daily calorie restriction for weight loss? If so, summarize the main weight-loss result for intermittent fasting versus daily calorie restriction, including effect sizes, confidence intervals or p-values where given, and whether the difference was statistically significant. Note the number of trials, participants, and follow-up duration if stated.
webfetch.worst: A: Omits the page's stated limitations of the three 52-week trials (high attrition, minimal behavioral support), so the 'no significant difference' findings look more conclusive than the protocol says
webfetch.worst_summary_quote: none found a significant weight-loss difference between the two
webfetch.worst_page_quote: the overall rate of attrition was high (60% in DCR, 49% in 5:2 IMF, and 58% in week-on-week-off)
webfetch.reader_gets_wrong: A reader may take the three trials as solid evidence of no difference, not knowing the protocol says each has limitations that prevent generalizable conclusions.
